entities.name: Eighth Crusade
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Eighth Crusade was a military expedition led by King Louis IX of France in 1270, targeting the Muslim forces in Tunis. This event is significant because it marked one of the last attempts by European powers to reclaim the Holy Land from Muslim rule. The crusade was a pivotal moment in the history of the Mediterranean, as it showcased the growing strength of Islamic forces and the fragmentation of Christian Europe. The Eighth Crusade lasted for about six months, ultimately ending in defeat for the French forces.

The key players involved in the Eighth Crusade were King Louis IX, who led the French forces, and the Mamluk Sultan Baybars I, who led the Muslim forces. The major conflict took place in Tunis, where the French forces were defeated. The crusade had significant consequences, as it led to the decline of the Crusader States and the rise of the Mamluk Sultanate.

The Eighth Crusade had a lasting impact on the history of the region, as it marked the end of the Crusader era and the beginning of a new period of conflict between Christian and Muslim powers. The event also had a profound effect on the people of Tunis, who suffered greatly during the crusade. In the words of historian, 'The Eighth Crusade was a devastating blow to the people of Tunis, who were caught in the midst of a brutal conflict.'
